history.summary: IDENTITY UNCERTAIN / PROVISIONAL. No web footprint was found for a distinct temple named 'Shree Ramkund Temple' in Bhuj; this entry is a thin placeholder. The name most likely refers to the Ramkund Stepwell near Hamirsar Lake and the Kutch Museum - a square, 56-foot carved stepwell with walls depicting the ten avatars of Vishnu and figures from the Ramayana (Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Hanuman) - and/or the Ram Dhun Temple adjoining it, where continuous chanting of 'Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram' has been maintained since January 1984 (suspended after the 2001 earthquake, which damaged the temple, and resumed for daytime hours from November 2001). Construction dates, patron and deity details are all unverified. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds 'Bhuj', which is the town; the real state is Gujarat (district Kutch). Coordinates are approximate to the Ramkund Road locality only.

name: Shree Ramkund Temple
town_description: Bhuj is the historic walled capital of Kutch in western Gujarat, rebuilt after the devastating 26 January 2001 earthquake. It centres on Hamirsar Lake and is known for the Swaminarayan Mandir, Aina Mahal, Prag Mahal, the Kutch Museum and as the gateway to the Rann of Kutch.
